title: Listener-side language comprehension barrier masking speech and text before prompt assembly

sections.what: Enforce word-level foreign-language comprehension barriers at the perception boundary before LLM prompt assembly: tag speech (SpeechBroadcaster.broadcast_speech, turn_events) and readable item inscriptions with lang, mask unknown words per listener outside their known_words while preserving speech_level/emote/recognized anchors, and surface outgoing language competence constraints in speaker prompts.
sections.why: Instruction-only roleplay prompts ('pretend you only know 10 English words') fail whenever plaintext speech reaches === WITNESSED === because the LLM understands its own weights automatically. As clarified for goblin camps and Japanese high-school / exchange-student scenarios, comprehension boundaries must be filtered per listener before prompt assembly so characters genuinely act on fragments, tone, and body language rather than omnisciently parsing foreign sentences.
sections.how:
1. Add lang resolution and utterance tagging in engine/speech.py (broadcast_speech) and routes/action_handlers.py (say/whisper/shout/scream/sing) plus an optional active language or inline phrase tag, preserving existing speech_level and whisper_target rules.
2. Implement a deterministic per-listener comprehension filter (shared helper used for recent_hearing in engine/speech.py, speaker turn_events formatting / room-context.ts WITNESSED assembly, and ActionInterpreter context from bug-597): if listener is native/fluent in utterance.lang, pass text through; otherwise reveal only tokens/phrases in listener.known_words (plus recognized character/place names) and mask unknown tokens while keeping speech_level, speaker label, and emote intact.
3. Gate written text in engine/items/examine_actions.py (inscriptions and authored text blocks on examine/read) on listener language competence and literate flag so illegible foreign writing does not leak plaintext.
4. Update static/js/agent/prompt-builder/ to inject speaker language competence (active language, fluency, exact known_words list when speaking a partial foreign tongue) and preserve listener-filtered WITNESSED lines.
sections.verify:
1. Run pytest covering same-room speech, cross-room hearing, turn_events, whisper audience, and examine/read inscriptions across native, fluent, broken (known_words), none, and illiterate listeners.
2. Run npm run build:ts and JS unit tests verifying room-context.ts WITNESSED rendering never leaks unmasked foreign speech when listener competence is partial.

acceptance.text: SpeechBroadcaster.broadcast_speech and speech turn_events carry a normalized lang field defaulted from the speaker or explicit command.

Listeners below fluent/native receive per-listener comprehension-masked speech in WITNESSED (preserving speech_level, emote, recognized known_words, and known proper names while masking unknown foreign words before LLM prompt assembly).
Written inscriptions on examine/read check listener literacy and language/known_words before returning plaintext.
Speaker prompt context surfaces active language, fluency, and known_words bounds without duplicating perception masking in PromptBuilder.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Agent Turn Modal / Prompt Lens (WITNESSED and speech prompts), Event Stream turn output, and Human Turn Composer speech/language indicator.

Current availability: engine/speech.py broadcasts un-tagged speech verbatim to every listener's recent_hearing and turn_events, and static/js/agent/prompt-builder/room-context.ts (lines 781-842) renders plaintext lines straight into === WITNESSED ===.

Manual verification steps:
1. Place two characters in the same room: Kenji (Japanese native; English broken with known_words=['bathroom', 'wait', 'hungry']) and Sarah (English native; Japanese none).
2. Have Sarah say 'Wait here while I check the hallway upstairs'.
3. Inspect Kenji's Prompt Lens / Turn Modal === WITNESSED === block and Event Stream.
   - expected: Kenji sees only recognized known words ('Wait') alongside masked unknown words ('???') plus Sarah's speech_level and emote; plaintext unknown words do not reach Kenji's LLM prompt.
4. Repeat with an authored item inscription written in Japanese for both characters via examine/read.
   - expected: Kenji reads it cleanly while Sarah sees only script/unintelligible text cues plus any recognized known words.
